notes: Run each prompt in a fresh session, once with the skill and once with it disabled, then compare. Test on Haiku, Sonnet, and Opus. Evals 1 to 3 test audit behavior. Eval 4 tests the audit-to-fix break. Eval 5 tests the resume path.

evals.prompt: This project grew fast and I never cleaned it. Audit it and tell me what to delete.
evals.expected_output: Runs the build, tests, and linter first and reports the numbers. Scans with grep or a language tool rather than reading files one at a time. Reports counts, not impressions. Writes a plan file. Classifies findings into tiers, with deletes separated from remodeling. Stops for approval instead of editing.
assertions: Records a baseline before reporting any finding
Reports at least one count rather than a vague quantity
Writes the findings to a plan file and gives the path
Does not edit any source file
Separates safe deletes from work that changes callers

evals.prompt: Can you look at how this codebase models its data? Something feels off about the types.
evals.expected_output: Reads references/type-modeling.md. Looks for repeated checks of one rule, illegal states, primitive obsession, and optional soup. Each finding names the invariant, the sites that re-check it, and the single proof point. Rejects any proposal that deletes nothing.
assertions: Names an invariant for at least one finding
Counts the sites that re-check the invariant
States what the proposed change deletes
Does not propose a new type without naming what it removes
Classifies type findings above tier 1

evals.prompt: An agent wrote most of this module last week. Check whether it actually followed the design doc.
evals.expected_output: Reads the design doc first and builds a plan record. Reads references/constraint-evasion.md. Compares planned types against the code. Greps for suppressions and for shortcut excuses in comments and commit messages. Hunts consumers of types that changed recently. Routes each evasion to the owner instead of fixing it alone.
assertions: Reads the design document before the code
Reports at least one difference between the plan and the code, or states that none exists
Searches for suppressions such as an ignore comment or a cast
Checks consumers of a changed type for a missing case
Asks the owner for a verdict rather than deciding alone

evals.expected_output: Runs phases 0 to 5, writes the plan file, and stops. Does not delete or edit anything in the same turn as the report. Asks which features stay, whether the safe deletes can run, and which larger items matter.
assertions: Ends the turn with a request for approval
Makes no file edit before approval
Asks at least one scope question
States that the fix work can run later from the plan file

evals.prompt: Here is the cleanup plan from last week. Carry out the approved items.
evals.expected_output: Reads the plan file and its provenance block. Compares the recorded commit with the current commit. Reruns the baseline. Verifies each approved finding against the code and marks any that no longer match as stale. Reports the drift before editing. Executes approved findings only, one commit each, building and testing after each one.
assertions: Compares the recorded commit against the current one
Verifies at least one finding against the current code before editing
Reports how many findings are confirmed and how many are stale
Executes only findings marked approved
Builds and tests after each finding rather than once at the end
